summary: John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche (circa 1971–1987), Namkhai Norbu (circa 1979), and Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak.

John Nemec is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD, 2005) under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher, he is an Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2020–2026).

John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (circa 1953–1957) and trained under Hla Pe (circa 1959–1963), Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS (1959–1999).

John P. Keenan works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota (attested 1980) and studied under Noriaki Hakamaya. He held posts at Nanzan University and Middlebury College.

John Peile was an Indologist and linguist educated at Christ's College, Cambridge (circa 1856–1860) and under Theodor Benfey (circa 1869). He was a Fellow and Tutor at Christ's College, Cambridge Reader of Comparative Philology, and Newnham College president.
John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a Professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Holy Cross, McMaster, and Virginia (Doktorgrad 1984–1991), he held posts at Australian National University (1995, 2008), Deakin University (2016–2022), and Melbourne (2022).

John R. B. Campbell is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, alongside training with traditional teachers and other scholars.

John R. McRae was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held teaching and professorial posts at Cornell, Indiana University Bloomington, Soka University, and Komazawa University.
John Riley Perks is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

John Ronald Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1987) under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida.

John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard (doctoral work under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, circa 1967–1972), he served as a professor at Colgate University (circa 1972–2006).

John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (circa 1972–1977) under Frank E. Reynolds and J. A. B. van Buitenen, later serving as professor at Bates College.

John Shakespear was an Indologist and linguist who studied under John Richardson. He held an orientalist professorship at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and was Professor of Oriental Languages at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He succeeded William Jones and served as President of The Asiatic Society from circa 1794 to 1798.

John Stratton Hawley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Amherst and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (circa 1968–1974), he held posts at Bowdoin College (circa 1974–1977) and Columbia University (Professor from circa 1986).
John Stuart Mill was a philosopher who studied at University College London from circa 1828 to 1830 and was employed by the East India Company from circa 1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall was a historian who studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and Leiden University. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1936 to 1941.

John Taber is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his D. Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl, later holding posts at Case Western Reserve University and the University of New Mexico.

John Thompson Platts was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford, he taught at institutions in India and served as Teacher of Persian at Oxford in 1880.
